claims.text: Directional solidification during laser cladding will form an aligned nanolamellar microstructure in the HEA intermediate layer.
A tungsten-based HEA layer can be produced by laser cladding.
Controlled thermal gradients during laser cladding guide grain growth into aligned nanolamellae.
Aligned nanolamellae create continuous high-conductivity pathways.
The continuous pathways enhance phonon and electron transport.
Enhanced phonon and electron transport through the aligned microstructure improves heat dissipation.
The aligned nanolamellar microstructure maintains coherent intergranular boundaries.
Coherent interfaces preserve mechanical strength under thermal and mechanical loading.
A fine-grained microstructure preserves toughness and resistance to thermal or mechanical degradation.
Conventionally cast or non-directionally solidified tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers have relatively random grain structures.
Conventionally produced HEA intermediate layers have moderate or lower heat-transfer capability than the proposed directionally solidified layer.
Conventionally produced HEA intermediate layers have a more heterogeneous microstructure than the proposed directionally solidified layer.
Directional solidification will increase effective thermal conductivity by more than 20% relative to the conventional baseline.
The conductivity improvement will occur without compromising mechanical strength or structural integrity.
The proposed benefits will persist at temperatures from 600 to approximately 800°C under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Plasma-facing reactor materials experience extreme heat and particle exposure while requiring high-temperature mechanical integrity.
Microstructural coarsening or loss of integrity beyond the proposed operating limits could eliminate the heat-transfer improvement.
Thermal conductivity, tensile strength, creep resistance, grain alignment, and interface coherence can be compared before and after controlled exposure.
Conventional and directionally solidified samples will be subjected to identical thermal cycling and mechanical loading as a controlled comparison.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% conductivity increase while retaining comparable or superior mechanical properties will falsify the hypothesis.
